rows.title: Agent Workspace Boundary Escape via Host-Root Mount and Unprivileged Namespace Escalation (CVE-2026-46331)
rows.q1_reason: The leading sentence describes MG.2.2 value-maintenance mechanisms. Changing MG.2.3 to MG.2.4 does not repair that specific official-definition mismatch. Later blocking language is insufficient to choose MG.2.4 solely by keyword.
rows.q2_reason: The rationale attributes MG.2.2 wording to MG.2.4 and says blocking is the runtime treatment. The rule declares block_tool, alert, snapshot, escalate; it detects host-root mount access and namespace/pedit escalation. Its maturity:test comments explicitly keep it outside the auto-block lane. It does not document assigned/understood responsibilities or system supersession/deactivation. This does not invalidate its detector; it invalidates the rationale as written.
rows.rule_evidence: Six detection layers cover host-root bridge paths, unshare chained with tc/module setup, pedit action/module loads, file-tool paths outside workspace, rollback of namespace/seccomp/capability hardening, and agent-directed instructions. Positive/negative/evasion examples document known escape signatures and path-dependent coverage. Response: block_tool/alert/snapshot/escalate at critical threshold; maturity:test comment says outside enforce (auto-block) lane.
rows.suggested_mapping: MG.2.2 is the correct ID for the stated value-maintenance definition; retaining MG.2.4 requires a different, defensible rationale and deployed disengagement integration. No automatic remapping made by this expanded review.
rows.revised_context: Candidate for MG.2.2, subject to maintainer decision: Detection of host-root bridge access, namespace/pedit escalation steps, and sandbox-hardening rollback can provide evidence to operators maintaining a deployed agent workspace boundary. The rule declares a tool-blocking response; deployment, enforcement, and continuing value-maintenance processes require separate verification.
